course_description: Analyzes formal models in computer science, including regular expressions, finite automata, contextfree grammars, pushdown automata and Turing machine.

course_learning_outcomes.text: acquire a fundamental understanding of the core concepts in automata theory and formal languages;
analyze and construct regular expressions to define regular languages, solve string-matching problems, and effectively describe their corresponding languages in natural language;
classify the different computing machines by discussing the different formal models;
design grammars and recognizers for different formal languages;
explain the principles of pushdown automata (PDAs) by determining the languages they recognize, and designing PDAs for given languages to model computational processes;
evaluate Turing machines by identifying their components, their operations, and the languages they recognize; and
demonstrate 21st century skills in all learning activities;
Acquire a fundamental understanding of the core concepts in automata theory and formal languages.
Analyze and construct regular expressions to define regular languages, solve string-matching problems, and effectively describe their corresponding languages in natural language.
Classify the different computing machines by discussing the different formal models.

topic_learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate understanding of automata theory and apply its concepts to solve computational problems, including recognition of regular and context-free languages.
Understand the concepts of regular expressions and apply them to define regular languages and solve string- matching problems.
Describe in plain English the language of regular expressions with straightforward descriptions.
Write regular expressions of given regular languages.
Recognize and describe the components of a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA), including states, alphabet, transitions, start state, and accepting states.
Identify the languages of given DFAs.
Construct DFAs based from the given language.
